ideas.name: SK Hynix Inc. (ADR)
ideas.thesis: SKHY appeared in all 6 overnight screening runs with unanimous high conviction — the strongest consensus signal in today's digest. A JPMorgan Overweight initiation (Sep 9) and BofA $250 price target frame a ~31–32% upside gap versus current levels (~$188), while a 40 trillion won buyback, Temasek sovereign capital injection, and SK Hynix's ~57% share of the HBM market provide structural support. The Sept 10 pullback of ~5.2% from recent highs near $199 is flagged across runs as a re-entry dislocation ahead of Micron's Sept 30 earnings, which will serve as a key DRAM sector read-through.
ideas.catalyst: Micron (MU) earnings Sep 30, 2026 as DRAM/HBM sector read-through; next KRX earnings cycle expected October 2026
ideas.edge: JPMorgan $245 PT + BofA $250 PT vs. ~$188 close implies ~31% upside; 5.2% post-JPMorgan-initiation pullback on Sept 10 creates dislocation; 40 trillion won buyback + Temasek injection are structural floors; controls ~57% of HBM market
ideas.bull_case: AI data center HBM demand is multi-year and supply-constrained; fresh institutional buy ratings combined with buyback and sovereign capital support mean any Micron upside surprise on Sept 30 could close the gap to $245–$250 analyst targets rapidly.
ideas.bear_case: SKHY ADR liquidity can be thin and options availability is uncertain; Q2 earnings already produced a ~9.6% miss-driven selloff, showing execution risk at elevated expectations, and a hawkish Fed hike on Sept 16 could weigh on high-multiple tech/semis across the board.

ideas.name: Energy Select Sector SPDR Fund
ideas.thesis: XLE appeared in 4 of 6 runs as the clearest macro hedge in this environment, with the energy sector up 37–43% YTD as the #1 performing S&P 500 sector on the back of a genuine war-driven supply shock — Iran/Ukraine refinery disruptions removing ~14 mb/d of supply, Brent above $100 (broke $100 on Sept 9), and diesel at a record $5.85/gal nationally. Crucially, XLE functions as a dual hedge: it benefits directly from energy inflation AND provides a buffer if the Sept 16 Fed hike (79.5% Kalshi probability) validates persistent inflation, pressuring the rest of equities. Goldman Sachs warns Brent could average $100+ through 2026 if Hormuz stays restricted.
ideas.catalyst: FOMC rate decision Sep 16, 2026 — hike validates inflation/energy premium; ongoing Iran Strait of Hormuz supply disruption with no resolution timeline
ideas.edge: Energy sector +43% YTD, sector leadership confirmed; integrated majors at 8–12% FCF yields vs. market average; Goldman Sachs $100+ Brent average target; supply shock is war-driven and structurally unresolved — not a demand or sentiment story
ideas.bull_case: A Sept 16 hike validates the inflation-driven energy premium and could catalyze rotation from growth into energy; if Hormuz restrictions persist, Goldman's $100+ Brent average thesis keeps sector FCF yields elevated and dividends growing.
ideas.bear_case: XLE is up 30–43% YTD and a ceasefire or diplomatic resolution on Iran could trigger rapid mean reversion; a surprise Fed hold might spark a risk-on rotation away from defensive/commodity sectors into beaten-down tech.

ideas.name: Apple Inc.
ideas.thesis: AAPL appeared in 4 of 6 runs as a defined-risk options play on the well-documented post-iPhone-launch dip-and-recovery pattern, with the Sept 9 event dip already absorbed and the stock recovering toward ~$332. The foldable iPhone Duo (at $2,099–$2,299 ASP) represents a structurally new high-ASP product line with IDC forecasting >17M units shipped by 2027, generating $45.7B+ in segment value — a multi-quarter tailwind not yet priced into current models. BofA's $380 price target implies ~14% upside, and historical data shows AAPL gains in the 60-day post-event window 17 out of historical instances, with the window now open.
ideas.catalyst: iPhone 18 Pro / foldable iPhone Duo on sale Sep 19, 2026; Q4 FY2026 earnings (foldable demand data) late October 2026 under new CEO John Ternus
ideas.edge: BofA $380 PT (+14% from ~$332); Rothschild $400 PT (+20%); historical 60-day post-launch recovery in 17 of historical instances; foldable at $2,099–$2,299 is a new ASP expansion not modeled in consensus; post-event dip already absorbed at $332
